sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Passaic County, NJ?
sections.html:
Passaic County splits the work between its 16 municipalities and one county board. Each town assessor values property and each town collector bills it. The Passaic County Board of Taxation, created by legislation in 1909, certifies assessments, equalizes values for county tax purposes, prepares the abstract of ratables, certifies municipal tax rates and hears assessment appeals.

  • Board of Taxation: 930 Riverview Drive, Suite 250, Totowa, NJ 07512, phone (973) 720-7399.
  • Appeal hearings: 930 Riverview Drive, Suite 200, Totowa, starting at 9 a.m.
  • Town assessor: valuation, deductions, added and omitted assessments.
  • Town collector: bills, payments and tax payoff letters for a sale.

Anyone selling a Passaic County house starts with the collector in the town where the house stands, since the county board does not bill or collect.

sections.h2: What makes Passaic County different from other New Jersey counties?
sections.html:
Passaic County is small and dense. It has 186.01 square miles of land and about 2,818 people per square mile in the 2020 Census, against roughly 1,014 per square mile in Ocean County. The 2025 Census estimate is 531,624 residents in 186,341 housing units.

The county was created on February 7, 1837 from parts of Bergen and Essex counties. Its southeastern half is flat or gently hilly along the Passaic and Pompton Rivers, while the northwest is rugged highland, with West Milford covering 80.32 square miles, more than 40% of the county's area. Paterson, the county seat, holds more than 30% of the population.

Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 shows a median owner-occupied value of $459,500, a median household income of $87,522 and an owner-occupied rate of 53.1%. About a third of residents were born outside the United States, and 51.3% speak a language other than English at home. A seller here may be dealing with a two-family house, a rental building or a hillside single-family home in the same county, and the tax picture changes with each.

sections.h2: What are the Passaic County tax appeal deadlines?
sections.html:
A regular petition of appeal is due on or before April 1, and the board's 2026 notice said not to file before February 1, after the assessment card arrives. Towns that completed a revaluation or reassessment get May 1, and for 2026 the county named Paterson as that town. Added and omitted assessments have their own later deadline.

Passaic County Board of Taxation filing dates for the 2026 appeal year
Type of appealWho it coversLast day to file
Regular petitionMost townsApril 1, 2026
Regular petition after revaluation or reassessmentPaterson for 2026May 1, 2026
Added or omitted assessmentAll 16 municipalitiesDecember 1, 2026

The same pattern repeats each year, so the dates for later years follow the April 1, May 1 and December 1 rule.

sections.h2: How does a Passaic County appeal work once it is filed?
sections.html:
The appeal challenges the assessed value, not the tax rate, and the burden is on the owner to prove the value was wrong as of the October 1 before the tax year.

  • Bring recent sales of similar homes near the October 1 date, with photographs and a property record card from the town assessor.
  • Appeals over $1,000,000 of assessed value may go straight to the Tax Court of New Jersey.
  • A county board judgment can be taken to Tax Court within 45 days of the date of the judgment.
  • Added or omitted assessment bills are generally mailed in October and payable November 1, and an appeal of one must be filed before December 1.

Paterson's assessor page explains how added assessments work, and the rule is statewide: new construction or an addition finished after October 1 is valued as of the first of the following month and taxed for the full months left in the year. A seller who built a new deck, a finished basement or an extension should expect the assessor to notice.

sections.h2: How do roads and rivers shape a Passaic County sale?
sections.html:
Interstate 80 and Interstate 287 cross the county near Paterson, and the Garden State Parkway cuts across the southern end near Clifton. The Passaic River is the county's main waterway, and the southeastern half of the county is flat or only mildly hilly along it and the Pompton River. The Passaic River winds northeast past Totowa into Paterson and then turns south toward Newark, and the lowest point in the county, about 20 feet above sea level, sits along that river in Clifton.

Paterson's average winter low is 19 degrees in January and its summer high reaches 86 in July, with about 2.9 to 4.8 inches of rain a month, so roofs, gutters and basements take real wear. A seller in a river town does well to gather repair records and any flood history before the first showing. Ask the town building department about open permits before you list.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Passaic County property tax?
sections.html:
Late installments carry interest set by each town, up to 8% on the first $1,500 and 18% beyond it. If the town holds a lien, a standard tax sale follows in the next fiscal year, and an accelerated sale is allowed once the debt is still open on the 11th day of the eleventh month. The statute lets a town leave out of the sale any property whose owner is paying a signed plan in equal monthly installments that clears the debt within five years.

A delinquency of more than $10,000 can also draw a year-end penalty of up to 6% where the town has adopted one. A seller with tax owing should ask the collector for the exact number on the closing date, because interest runs each day until payment.

Relief programs run through the state. Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ share one application; the 2025 filing deadline of November 2, 2026 has passed, so owners should look at the Division of Taxation page for the next cycle.

sections.h2: What does recording a Passaic County sale cost?
sections.html:
The Passaic County Clerk records deeds and mortgages. The county's fee schedule lists a deed at $45 for the first page and $10 for each added page, a mortgage at $35 for the first page, and a notice of settlement at $20 for two parties. A mortgage cancellation is $25, and an inheritance tax waiver is $15.

The same schedule publishes a realty transfer tax table. For a sale of $350,000 or less the regular rate is $4.00 per $1,000 up to $150,000, $6.70 per $1,000 from there to $200,000, and $7.80 per $1,000 up to $350,000. Above $350,000 the rates start at $5.80 per $1,000 and climb in steps to $12.10 per $1,000 above $1,000,000. Senior citizen rates are lower. Your closing agent will confirm which column applies.

faqs.q: Where is the Passaic County Board of Taxation?
faqs.a: It is at 930 Riverview Drive, Suite 250, Totowa, NJ 07512, and the phone is (973) 720-7399. Appeal hearings are held in Suite 200 at the same address, starting at 9 a.m.

faqs.q: When is the Passaic County tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 for a regular petition, May 1 for a town that did a revaluation or reassessment (Paterson in 2026), and December 1 for added or omitted assessments. File no earlier than February 1 of the tax year, after your assessment card arrives.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax in Passaic County, the county or the town?
faqs.a: You pay your town's tax collector. The county board certifies and hears appeals, but the town bills and collects for municipal, school and county levies together.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Passaic County assessment on my own?
faqs.a: Yes. Individual owners may represent themselves at the county board, while business entities other than sole proprietorships need an attorney. Large properties over $1,000,000 can file directly with the Tax Court of New Jersey.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Passaic County house with tax owing?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, plus interest to the closing date, is settled from the sale proceeds. Ask the town collector for a written payoff, and ask whether any tax sale certificate has been issued on the parcel.
